transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time with my eating. What scares me is that once I start eating—especially when I’m alone in the kitchen—it just feels like I’ve stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop. I'll be telling myself the whole time, ‘Janet, put it away,’ but I just can't seem to do it.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating?

Yes. Afterward, I just... I feel awful about myself. It's like I’ve wasted food that I actually meant to share. And I just think, I’m too old to be acting this way. I usually just sit there feeling ashamed, and I promise myself it won’t happen again.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a minute ago, that's actually the part that scares me the most. Once I start, especially if I'm by myself in the kitchen, it really just feels like I've stepped aside. I'm completely aware of what's happening, and my brain is telling me, 'Janet, put it away,' but... I just can't make myself stop. I have zero control over it.
During these episodes, do you think you're eating an amount of food that's significantly more than what most people would eat under similar circumstances?

Yes, I do. It's definitely more than what's normal. Like, on some afternoons after I finish my shift at the food bank, or maybe after I've been baking for an event at the senior center, I'll come home and just... keep going. I'll eat a full plate of leftovers, and then I'll have a few slices of banana bread, some chips, cheese, and whatever cookies are left in the tin. When it's all over, I look at the wrappers and empty plates and realize it was way, way more food than I would ever serve to another person for a meal.
How often do these episodes of eating happen to you?

Well, if I look back at my kitchen calendar and my schedule for the food bank weeks... I'd say these episodes have been happening most weeks. It's usually once or maybe twice a week. And it's been going on like that for many months now.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that. I just... I feel terrible afterward, but I don't throw up or take anything. And I'm definitely not one to go exercise for hours to burn it off. I just deal with feeling full and upset.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
No, I haven't really noticed any big changes. My clothes still fit about the same as they usually do, so I don't think my weight has fluctuated much one way or the other.
Do you ever eat large amounts of food in a short time when you're not even hungry?

Yes, I do. A lot of times, this happens after I’ve already had supper. My stomach isn’t asking for anything—I'm not hungry at all—but I still go back to the pantry or the fridge. I just keep picking at things... and it just turns into eating a lot.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're eating really quickly?

Yes, definitely. I catch myself eating so fast that I barely even taste what I'm having, like the casserole or the muffins I just made. I'll just stand right there at the kitchen counter, taking bite after bite... almost like I’m in a big hurry, even when there’s absolutely nowhere I need to be.
